title: Archibald Glasgow, maltman in Leith: testament testamentar, 1662
record: National Records of Scotland, Edinburgh Commissary Court, CC8/8/70, images 689-693
coverage: All five original images visually inspected, opening also enlarged. Substantial selective, non-continuous working extracts, not a complete diplomatic transcription. Archibald's entry begins near the foot of image 689 and concludes at the top of image 693. Preceding and following testaments excluded; financial lists and legal formulas only partly transcribed. Brackets mark uncertainty or omissions; some abbreviations expanded.

plain_english: Archibald Glasgow was a maltman living in Leith. He died in February 1662; confirmation is dated 24 May 1662 in the margin.

His widow Agnes Watson supplied the remaining estate information on behalf of the minor children. Archibald, George and William are explicitly called his lawful sons in the will and appointed executors.
Agnes is appointed to administer the property and act as tutor during the children's minority, assisted by Captain George Cock and Thomas Glasgow, weaver in Edinburgh.
The inventory includes twelve bolls of malt, eight bolls of bere, household furnishings and clothing. The accounts include money owed to and by the estate and costs of medicine during his illness.
William Glasgow, weaver in Leith, occurs as a creditor. His relationship to the testator is not stated in the inspected wording.
The will provides for paying debts and dividing the remaining property equally among the three children.
findings: Explicit spouse: Agnes Watson, described as relict spouse and later as his well-beloved spouse.
Explicit sons: Archibald, George and William Glasgow. Their sonship is stated separately from their executor appointments.
Thomas Glasgow, weaver in Edinburgh, is an overseer, writer of the will and named in the caution/confirmation passage. No brother relationship is securely stated.
Captain George Cock is an overseer, not thereby a relative. William Glasgow of Leith is a creditor, not thereby a brother or son.
The testament alone does not establish that this maltman was the shoemaker of the 1647 retour; existing profile association requires the wider maintained evidence.

The saved inventory quotation switches the subject to William Glasgow. The inventory opening on image 690 names Archibald Glasgow.
The sons' names and Agnes Watson's role are supported by original-image inspection, not solely the inherited quotation.
